answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to one hardware-backed key and a slow vesting history: a new agent earns nothing until it completes a chain of verified tasks over several epochs, like crossing a jade valley, a frozen tundra, and an umber desert in sequence. Each step costs real compute and time, and rewards vest only after the chain finishes, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must pay that full cost thousands of times while honest agents pay it once.
